problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/7523d27fa1aad56d67cb40a47715cc42d1f371c209ab4a9e5aef15413bc69490.png)

Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}{x}^{2}\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the right one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/b5be03a534691cfbd06178623d5a9dc802ff8814159635b4e4bf2b2693da167c.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le 3-x-z},
$$

where

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063571/assets/365451aa395e91cee59199b048ed59ce1fba2ee8ee569fc460ef8fe9bf3bcdfd.png)

Hence, the type III representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 3-x-z}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3-x-z}{x}^{2}\,dy\,dz\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3-x-z}{x}^{2}\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{3-x-z}{x}^{2}\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}[y]_{y=0}^{y=3-x-z}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}(3-x-z)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(3{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}z)\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}(3{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}z)\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}(3{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}z)\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[3{x}^{2}z-{x}^{3}z-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{z}^{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(3{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2})\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(3{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2})\,dx & ={[{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{6}{x}^{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{7}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Notice that our solid can be written as the type III region

R={(x,y,z):(x,z)∈D,0≤y≤3−x−z},

where

D={(x,z):0≤x≤1,0≤z≤1}

is the projection of R onto the xz-plane, shown below.

Hence, the type III representation of R is

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤1,0≤z≤1,0≤y≤3−x−z}

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

∭Rx2dV=∫01∫01∫03−x−zx2dydzdx.

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to y, treating x and z as constants:

∫01∫01∫03−x−zx2dydzdx=∫01∫01[∫03−x−zx2dy]dzdx=∫01∫01x2[y]y=0y=3−x−zdzdx=∫01∫01x2(3−x−z)dzdx=∫01∫01(3x2−x3−x2z)dzdx

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to z, treating x as a constant:

∫01∫01(3x2−x3−x2z)dzdx=∫01[∫01(3x2−x3−x2z)dz]dx=∫01[3x2z−x3z−12x2z2]z=0z=1dx=∫01(3x2−x3−12x2)dx

Finally, we integrate with respect to x:

∫01(3x2−x3−12x2)dx=[x3−14x4−16x3]x=0x=1=1−14−16=712.
